newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault, Peugeot fall amid gloom on outlook.
newsitem.headline: Renault, Peugeot fall amid gloom on outlook.

text.p: Shares in automakers Peugeot and Renault were down sharply in mid-afternoon amid worry over their sales outlook ahead of the September 30 expiry of government car buying incentive measures.
At 1345 GMT, Peugeot shares were off 18 francs or 3.10 percent at 562 while Renault shares were off 4.7 francs or 3.69 percent at 122.50.

"People are just gloomy about the outlook for the car market. There don't seem to be too many positives at the moment," said one trader. The government announced on Thursday it would not extend its new cars for old rebate programme beyond its expiry on September 30.

Earlier this month, Renault reported its profit shrank to 158 million francs in the first six months of the year from 1.76 billion a year earlier in the face of persistent weakness in the European car market and a price war that has eroded its profit margins.
Peugeot's profit for the first half tumbled by more than half.
